# Cipi

> Cipi is a Laravel-first open-source deploy CLI that also supports static sites and generic PHP apps. One command installs a complete production stack (Nginx, PHP, MariaDB, Valkey; optional PostgreSQL) on any Ubuntu VPS. It is CLI-first, with an optional self-hosted web control panel (GUI) you can install if you want a browser dashboard. MIT licensed, self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge.

Full plain-text site content for LLM ingestion: https://cipi.sh/llms-full.txt

## Site

English only. Public URLs have no language prefix: homepage `https://cipi.sh/`, docs `https://cipi.sh/docs/`, and so on. `/en/…` 301s to the same path without `/en`. Former language trees (`/de`, `/fr`, `/it`, `/es`, `/pt`) and localized slugs 301 to the English equivalent. There is no Accept-Language or cookie redirect.

Key facts:

- Install: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash`
- Admin access: SSH as `cipi` user, then `sudo cipi …` (no password, `cipi` only) or `su root` with the root password from the installation summary — not `sudo -s` (the `cipi` user's password is random and never shown)
- Optional web GUI: `cipi gui <domain>` installs an opt-in Laravel control panel to manage one or more servers from the browser; Cipi stays fully usable CLI-only without it. GUI supports Node apps, app/path redirects, prefix proxies, deploy audit, Meilisearch, fix-permissions, read-only Node runtimes / packages / monitor / Zero Trust (API 1.31+ / Cipi 5.4.1+) and Server → Disk (panel 3.1, API 1.33+ / Cipi 5.5.2+, ability disk-view), .env / auth.json / Artisan / App commands (API 1.14+ / Cipi 5.0.3+), server cockpit — PHP, SSH, services, SMTP, health, IP whitelist (API 1.15+ / Cipi 5.0.6+), Octane create (API 1.13+ / Cipi 5.0+), and multi-engine MariaDB/PostgreSQL (API 1.12+ / Cipi 4.8+)
- Current release: Cipi **5.5.2**, panel API **1.33.0**. 5.5.2 regenerates `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api` so the panel may run `cipi disk` and `cipi disk *`. API 1.33 adds `GET /api/disk` and `GET /api/disk/dbs` (`disk-view`; MCP `DiskUsage`, `DiskDatabases`; 73 tools); `cipi-cli disk` (1.6.0) and the GUI Server → Disk tab read them. The same release aligns `cipi.yml` with the server: `deploy.node_build` is the Laravel asset build before the release goes live (`deploy.post` runs after), `deploy.predeploy_snapshot` is the pre-deploy snapshot (`snapshot` still accepted), `cipi yml generate --save` writes `/home/<app>/cipi.yml` (apply still reads the committed copy), backup profiles the file drops leave the schedule (archives stay for `cipi backup prune`), and the deploy-success mail quotes the auto-apply result. API 1.32 adds `GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/limits` (including soft `disk_limit_gb`), `GET|PUT /api/ssl/dns` and `DELETE /api/ssl/dns/{account}`, an optional DNS-01/wildcard body on `POST /api/apps/{name}/ssl`, and `type` (`laravel`|`custom`|`node`) plus `custom` and `docroot` on app list/show. 5.5.1 makes wildcard certificates work end to end: Cipi writes the HTTPS vhost itself and certbot only issues/renews (`certbot install --nginx` cannot be driven non-interactively for a `*.` name), every tenant is redirected to HTTPS, Cloudflare Origin CA works on any app, a DNS-01 certificate is reissued over DNS-01 (`--http` to go back), certificate names drop what a wildcard covers, renewals reload nginx (certbot deploy hook) and no longer force `--nginx`, `cipi ssl status` shows per app the names not covered, `cipi app list` no longer shows PHP-FPM apps as Octane. 5.5.0 adds **`cipi disk [--json]`** (every filesystem, then every app largest first: files = the app's home, database = the app's DB plus the one in `DB_DATABASE` if different, total, % of the disk holding /home; `All apps` and `Everything else` rows; sizes below 0.01 GB in MB; JSON has `files_kb`, `database_kb`, `total_kb`, `limit_gb`, `limit_percent`, `over_limit`; measured with `du` on demand, nothing stored) and **`cipi disk db [--json]`** (MariaDB and PostgreSQL per database in MB, Valkey per logical db with key counts plus instance memory and disk, Meilisearch per index with document counts plus `data.ms`; whole-engine size on disk; uninstalled engines left out); **soft per-app disk limits** — `cipi app limits <app> --disk=<GB>|none`, default none, files + database, never blocks, stored as `disk_limit_gb` outside the `limits` object that cipi.yml reconciles (a repository cannot raise its own quota), carried by `cipi sync`; new monitor check **`app_disk`** (on by default, only measures apps with a limit, warn at 90%, crit when over, per-app alert state, measurement reused for 30 min, `cipi monitor set app_disk --warn= --minutes=`, trigger `monitor_app_disk`); **`cipi firewall attempts [<1-100>|default]`** — fail2ban `[sshd] maxretry` (default 3, 1-hour window, 24 h ban growing to 7 days, recidive unchanged) in `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/cipi-attempts.local`, validated with `fail2ban-client -t` and rolled back if refused, never reset by updates, added to `cipi compliance report` evidence; **`cipi ssh apps [--json]`**, `cipi ssh apps enable|disable <app>|--all` — app users in group `cipi-nossh` are denied SSH/SFTP from non-local addresses by one `Match Group cipi-nossh Address *,!127.0.0.1,!::1` → `DenyUsers *` block (validated with `sshd -t`, reload not restart, checked with `sshd -T -C`); deploys over `ssh localhost` keep working; `--all` also sets the default for new apps and `cipi sync import`; `cipi`/`root` refused; trigger `app_ssh_access`; default every app user enabled; **several Cloudflare accounts for DNS-01** — `cipi ssl dns set [--name=NAME] --token=` (default account stays `/etc/cipi/cloudflare.ini`, named ones in `/etc/cipi/cloudflare/`, root-only, re-running rotates), `cipi ssl install <app> --dns=cloudflare --account=NAME [--wildcard]` (account kept on reissue, unknown accounts refused before certbot), `cipi ssl dns list [--json]`, `cipi ssl dns remove <NAME>` (refused while a certificate renews with it); renewals use each certificate's own credentials file; `cipi ssl status` names the account. **Fixed in 5.5.0:** Laravel logs were rotated twice and never expired (`LOG_CHANNEL=daily` + logrotate left `laravel-<date>.log.1` uncompressed forever and an empty `laravel-<date>.log` that `cipi app logs --type=laravel` read) — new apps get `LOG_CHANNEL=single`, logrotate pattern `storage/logs/*[!0-9].log` (daily, compressed from day 2, 365 rotations); tab-completion now works after `sudo cipi` without bash-completion (`_cipi_sudo_complete`), in non-login shells via a `~/.bashrc` loader for root and cipi, and with app names from the `cipi-apps` group; `setup.sh` detects containers and shared-kernel virtualization (OpenVZ/Virtuozzo, LXC, Docker, Podman, WSL, OrbStack, systemd-nspawn) and names them instead of failing with `requires Ubuntu 24.04+ (found: 24.04)`, and the version check no longer needs `bc`. Migration 5.5.0 (Laravel apps only): rewrites `/etc/logrotate.d/cipi-app-logs`; switches `LOG_CHANNEL=daily` (and `daily` inside `LOG_STACK`) to `single` via an atomic rename as the app user; where the .env changed runs `artisan config:cache` if cached, SIGTERMs running Supervisor programs (workers, Horizon, Octane, Reverb restart gracefully) and reloads PHP-FPM once per version; folds dated logs (`.log`, `.log.N`, `.log.N.gz`) into `laravel.log`, oldest first, never replacing it; idempotent. 5.4.1 opens redirects, proxies and Node apps to the panel: `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api` lets `www-data` run `cipi redirect set|enable|disable|unset|add|remove|list`, `cipi proxy add|remove|list` and `cipi node list|status|restart` (exact command lines); Node runtime management (`node install|default|upgrade|remove`), `search install|upgrade|key-rotate`, `package install|remove` and every `zt` mutation stay CLI-root; migration 5.4.1 regenerates the file and checks it with `visudo -cf`. 5.4.0 adds **Node apps** — `cipi app create --node=spa|static|ssr [--framework=next|nuxt|sveltekit|astro|remix|vite] [--node-version=22|24] [--build=] [--start=] [--output=] [--health-path=]`: spa (nginx serves current/<output>, fallback /index.html, immutable asset dirs, no-cache html), static (no fallback, real 404 with /404.html), ssr (nginx upstream /etc/nginx/conf.d/cipi-node-<app>.conf, WebSocket, X-Forwarded-*); blue/green SSR via root `cipi-node-switch` (Supervisor `<app>-node-blue|green` on localhost ports 3100–3999, health path must answer below 500 within 60 s, then the upstream moves and the old slot drains; a failure keeps the old slot and fails the deploy before `current` moves; rollback switches back); `cipi-node-run` reads .env as data, forces HOST/HOSTNAME/NITRO_HOST=127.0.0.1 and runs the start command as argv with a Node runner only; the recipe installs from the lockfile (npm ci, pnpm/bun --frozen-lockfile, yarn --immutable) and builds with NODE_ENV=production; webhooks without cipi/agent via an on-demand PHP-FPM receiver (/usr/local/share/cipi/webhook.php: GitHub/Bitbucket HMAC, GitLab/Azure tokens, app branch only); `cipi node status|restart|logs <app>`; `cipi app edit --build= --start= --output= --health-path= --node-version= --node=`; `cipi sync` skips and `cipi app clone` refuses Node apps; no database is created. **`cipi node`** — `install|list|upgrade [--restart]|remove <major>`: official nodejs.org builds verified against SHASUMS256.txt in /opt/cipi/node, even majors only, corepack on; `cipi node default <major>|system` links node/npm/npx/corepack/pnpm/yarn into /usr/local/bin for Laravel `--node-build`, `cipi app run npm` and `deploy.post`; `cipi app edit <laravel-app> --node-version=24|default` pins one app; trigger `node_default`. **Deploy audit ledger** — the Deployer recipe calls root `cipi-deploy-audit` after deploy:symlink, on deploy:failed and after rollback; root reads the release, commit and releases_log from /proc plus the origin (cipi-cli, panel, webhook, app-web, app-queue, ssh, cron, root-shell), the audit login uid operator, SSH IP and process chain; app claims (`source`, `actor`, `ip`, `ref`, `request_id` from `~/.deploy-trigger.run` or `CIPI_DEPLOY_*`) are kept under `claimed`; `/var/log/cipi/deploys.jsonl` is root-only with a sequence number and the SHA-256 of the previous line, mirrored to syslog `cipi-deploy`; `cipi deploy <app> --audit [--days=90] [--json]`; `cipi compliance deploys` fails on a broken chain and warns on missing hooks or rules and on releases the ledger never saw. **cipi.yml** gains `app.www`, `app.basic_auth` (names or bcrypt/SHA-512 hashes, never passwords), `redirect`, `redirects[]`, `proxies[]` (no --force, no link-local/metadata upstreams), `node:` (applied by the deploy through `cipi yml node-sync`, needs `yml auto`), `search`, `deploy:` recipe options (keep_releases, migrate, optimize, storage_link, queue_restart, horizon_terminate, extra_artisan, snapshot), `app.limits` (out of bounds blocks the plan), `ssl.force_https` (on only), `env.required` (names only) and `crons:` (allowlisted runners, `# cipi-yml` tagged crontab lines). **Fixed in 5.4.0:** old backups were never deleted (the pre-5.1 layout and removed profiles are now pruned to the longest age-based retention; S3 listing/delete errors alert via `backup_fail` and make `cipi backup prune` exit 1; root's cron PATH includes /usr/local/bin); `cipi api update` notified every night; `cipi yml example` printed `every:: command not found`; workers/schedule in cipi.yml on a custom app now block the plan; basic auth user removal matched by regex. Migration 5.4.0 installs the audit helper, per-app sudoers rules and deploy.php hooks, switches the trigger cron to `mv`, and moves servers still on Node 20 (end of life April 2026) to `cipi node default 22` (NodeSource package kept; fresh installs get Node 22). 5.3.1 adds **`cipi compliance`** (read-only evidence for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A and SOC 2 audits — 17 controls, `report` bundle in /var/log/cipi/compliance with report.md, report.json, raw evidence, SHA256SUMS and a checksummed .tar.gz; no secrets exported) and **`cipi redirect`** / **`cipi proxy`** (app and path redirects, reverse proxy prefixes stored in apps.json, validated, rolled back if `nginx -t` fails; CLI only, no migration). 5.3.0 adds **Cloudflare Zero Trust** (`cipi zt`, opt-in — `setup.sh` and `cipi self-update` never install `cloudflared` or call `enable`): `cipi zt token set --token= --account=` (root-only `/etc/cipi/zt.token`; needs Account.Cloudflare Tunnel Edit, Account.Access: Apps and Policies Edit, Zone.DNS Edit, plus Zone.SSL and Certificates Edit for Origin CA; not `/etc/cipi/cloudflare.ini`, which stays certbot DNS-01); `enable` (official cloudflared package, locally-managed tunnel, systemd unit, nginx `real_ip` from `api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/ips` reading `CF-Connecting-IP`, fail2ban `ignoreip` backup of the ranges, CrowdSec allowlist when CrowdSec is on, daily `cipi zt refresh` cron; does **not** close 22/80/443); `hostname add <app|--gui>` (CNAME to `{tunnel-id}.cfargotunnel.com`, ingress `http://127.0.0.1:80`, public CDN/WAF, no Access; `cipi app create` does not add it, `cipi zt status` lists apps not on the tunnel); `access enable <app|--gui>` (Cloudflare Access, any authenticated user; a Bypass application for `/cipi/webhook` when the app has a Git webhook); `ssh enable --hostname=` (ingress `ssh://127.0.0.1:22` + Access SSH app, prints the `ProxyCommand cloudflared access ssh` config; port 22 stays open; Deployer still SSHs to localhost); `lock http [--yes]` (refuses while any app renews Let's Encrypt over HTTP-01, `--force` skips; closes 80/443 if every HTTP hostname is on the tunnel, else allows 80/443 only from Cloudflare ranges); `lock ssh [--yes]` (only if cloudflared is active and the tunnel has SSH ingress; rescue `cipi zt ssh unlock`); `origin-cert <app>` (optional 15-year Cloudflare Origin CA; marks the app so `cipi ssl install` HTTP-01 will not overwrite it); `status|disable|refresh|unlock http`; `disable` restores UFW 22/80/443, removes cloudflared and the tunnel, leaves Let's Encrypt alone. `cipi ssl install` HTTP-01 refuses under `lock http` and on Origin CA apps; tunneled apps get certbot `--no-redirect`; `cipi ssl force` refuses on them. Triggers `zt_enable`, `zt_disable`, `zt_lock_http`, `zt_lock_ssh`. 5.3.0 also adds **`cipi monitor`** — server checks every 5 minutes from `/etc/cron.d/cipi-monitor` (`/usr/local/bin/cipi-monitor`), state files in `/var/log/cipi/monitor/`, no metrics storage: `disk` (warn ≥80% / crit ≥90%), `ssl` (Let's Encrypt expiry ≤14 days), `services` (every installed Cipi service via systemd), `workers` (`*-worker-*` / `*-horizon` must be RUNNING), `http_5xx` (≥20 and ≥5% of requests in the bytes appended since the previous run; per-log offsets survive logrotate; first run only baselines), `fs` (`/etc/cipi` or `/var/log/cipi` read-only), `load` (>4× cores for 2 consecutive runs); edge-triggered (ok→fail once, warn↔crit once, recovery `monitor_ok`, reminder every `reminder_minutes`, default 240); `cipi monitor [--json]` exits 1 on warn/crit, `list`, `enable|disable <check>`, `set disk --warn= --crit=`, `set ssl --days=`, `set http_5xx --count= --ratio=`, `set load --factor= --runs=`, `set reminder --minutes=`, `test`; triggers `monitor_disk|ssl|services|workers|http_5xx|fs|load|ok`. And **alert channels**: `cipi notifications channel add <slack|discord|ntfy|telegram|webhook> <id> --url=` (Telegram `--token= --chat-id=`; ntfy `--priority=`), `list|remove|enable|disable|test <id|all>`, stored encrypted in `/etc/cipi/alerts.json`; every existing trigger fans out to chat as well as email (no SMTP needed for chat); 5-second timeout per channel, failures only logged to `events.log`; ntfy urgent triggers raised to high priority; Discord truncated at 2000 chars, Telegram at 4096; webhook JSON `{server, trigger, subject, body, ts}`; no channel = email-only as before. **Fixed in 5.3.0:** jq `// true` read an explicit `false` as true — `cipi notifications disable <trigger>` kept firing, `cipi smtp configure --tls=off` was ignored (msmtp always got `tls on`), and `health: {enabled: false}` in `cipi.yml` did nothing; now `!= false` / `has()`. Migration 5.3.0 installs the monitor cron and default `monitor.json` / `alerts.json`, regenerates panel API sudoers (`zt status`, `monitor list`; enable/lock/set stay CLI-only) and refreshes completion; it configures no channel and enables no Zero Trust. 5.2.3 extends `cipi git` beyond GitHub/GitLab: **Cursor Origin** (`origin.cursor.com`), **AWS CodeCommit** (`git-codecommit.*.amazonaws.com`), **Bitbucket Cloud** (`bitbucket.org`) and **Azure DevOps** (`dev.azure.com` / `ssh.dev.azure.com` / `*.visualstudio.com`) are detected from the SSH clone URL; `cipi git origin-token|bitbucket-token|azure-token|codecommit-token <access-key> <secret-key> <iam-user>` plus matching `remove-*`; deploy key always registered, webhook where the forge has one (Bitbucket `repo:push` + HMAC `secret`; Azure `git.push` service hook sending `X-Gitlab-Token`); Origin and CodeCommit have no per-repo HTTP webhook, so deploy with `cipi deploy`. CodeCommit uses IAM `UploadSSHPublicKey` via curl `--aws-sigv4`, mints a 4096-bit `id_rsa` (IAM refuses ed25519) and writes `~/.ssh/config` so the SSH Key ID is the username; IAM allows five SSH keys per user. New apps keyscan `bitbucket.org`, `origin.cursor.com`, `ssh.dev.azure.com` and the repository URL host. CrowdSec allowlists Bitbucket egress CIDRs from `ip-ranges.atlassian.com` (fail-open); Azure/Origin need `cipi crowdsec allow` if banned. 5.2.3 also adds **`deploy.post` in `cipi.yml`** — allowlisted post-deploy steps (`artisan`, `npm`/`npx`/`yarn`/`pnpm`, `composer`, one relative `php`/`node` script), no free shell, run on both `cipi deploy` and the webhook and **without** `cipi yml auto`; `deploy.post_on_failure: warn` (default, mails `yml_post_fail`) or `abort`; `cipi yml post-deploy <app>` runs them now. And **manual stack upgrades**: `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [mariadb|pgsql]`, `cipi service upgrade [nginx|mariadb|postgresql|valkey]` — patch-level only, `--yes` to skip the prompt, `all` refused, never on a cron, not granted by `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api`; shared `lib/stack-upgrade.sh`, lock `/run/cipi-stack-upgrade.lock`, mails `nginx_upgrade`/`mariadb_upgrade`/`pgsql_upgrade`/`valkey_upgrade`. **Security fix in 5.2.3:** a custom app serves `htdocs/` as document root, so a committed `cipi.yml` answered at `https://domain/cipi.yml`; every app vhost now denies `/cipi.yml` and `/cipi.yaml` at any path (Laravel included), applied on update without regenerating the vhost, and `cipi yml` also looks in `htdocs/`. 5.2.2 adds two more opt-in commands, neither installed by `setup.sh` or `cipi self-update`: **`cipi search`** (Meilisearch as a native binary for Laravel Scout — 127.0.0.1 only, Cipi-written `SCOUT_PREFIX`, app delete revokes the key, clone mints a new one) and **`cipi package`** (allowlisted apt for host binaries: image-optimizers, ffmpeg, imagemagick, poppler-utils; Chromium is refused because it would pull snapd). 5.2.0 adds **opt-in CrowdSec** and a **nightly integrity scan** — neither is installed by `setup.sh` or `cipi self-update`, and there is no WAF. `cipi crowdsec enable` installs the engine **and** a registered firewall bouncer (`crowdsec-firewall-bouncer-nftables|-iptables` via `cscli bouncers add`), reads `/home/*/logs/nginx-{access,error}.log`, refuses below 512MB MemAvailable or behind a reverse proxy without `set_real_ip_from`/`real_ip_header` (`--force` overrides), allowlists the current SSH session, and starts a rescue TLS listener whose one-shot token allowlists the TCP peer and unbans it in CrowdSec and fail2ban (`cipi crowdsec rescue token|rotate`, `allow|unallow`). `disable` flushes the CrowdSec chains before purging. Allowlists cover localhost, RFC1918, Let's Encrypt, GitHub webhook CIDRs from `api.github.com/meta` `.hooks` (fail-open) and hardcoded GitLab.com CIDRs dated 2026-09-07. `cipi ban list|unban` includes CrowdSec when the engine is up. `cipi scan` runs nightly at 04:40: sha256 integrity of `current/` (or `htdocs/`) against a manifest written at every deploy and rollback in `/var/lib/cipi/manifests` (root:root 0600), then one ClamAV pass over upload dirs only with rfxn PHP-webshell signatures; mails `scan_integrity` or `scan_incomplete` — never a false "clean". `enable` refuses below 2GB MemAvailable or 3GB free on `/var`. Bash and zsh tab-completion is installed automatically by `setup.sh` and every `self-update` (`cipi completion bash|zsh [--print]`). Migration 5.2.0 installs `cipi-scan-manifest` and the rescue helpers, creates the manifest store, grants per-app manifest sudo entries, and adds `SSH_CLIENT`/`SSH_CONNECTION` to `env_keep` in `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-sudo` (validated with `visudo -c`); it enables nothing. 5.2.1 added `cipi git refresh` and `cipi app fix-permissions`. 5.1.3 fixed `cipi ini list`; 5.1.2 made Laravel Reverb production-ready (generated credentials, `ws://`/`wss://` from the certificate, a proxy matching only `/app/{key}` and `/apps/{id}/…`, `workers.reverb` in `cipi.yml`); 5.1.1 repaired FPM pools and wildcard domains end to end
- Stack: Nginx, PHP 8.x, MariaDB (default), optional PostgreSQL, Valkey, Supervisor; optional Laravel Octane (FrankenPHP) beside FPM (v5.0+)
- Databases (v4.8.0+): MariaDB on 3306 + optional PostgreSQL on 5432; `cipi db install|uninstall|default|engines`; `--engine=mariadb|pgsql` on db/app commands
- www redirects (v4.8.0+): `cipi www add|force-to-root|force-from-root|clear|status`; `cipi ssl force` re-applies HTTPS redirect
- Backup profiles (v5.1.0+): `cipi backup profile add` — scope (all/files/db), schedule, dest (local/s3), retention, `--encrypt`; databases discovered from the engine (tenant DBs included); `cipi backup verify|status|fetch`; managed crontab block
- `cipi.yml` (v5.1.0+): optional per-project file for aliases, PHP, extra DBs, workers (Horizon; Reverb since 5.1.2), healthcheck, backups, and post-deploy steps (`deploy.post`, since 5.2.3); `cipi yml generate|plan|apply|auto|post-deploy`; looked up in `current/`, `shared/` and `htdocs/` (5.2.3), and never served over HTTP (5.2.3). Since 5.5.2: `deploy.node_build` (Laravel asset build before go-live), `deploy.predeploy_snapshot` (`snapshot` still accepted), `cipi yml generate --save` (writes `/home/<app>/cipi.yml`; apply reads the committed copy), dropped backup profiles this file created leave the schedule, and the deploy-success mail quotes the auto-apply result
- `cipi ini` (v5.1.0+): guided php.ini for FPM and CLI, server-wide or `--app=`; whitelist of settable keys
- Post-deploy healthchecks (v5.1.0+): verify the live release after every deploy; optional `--rollback-on-unhealthy` (does not undo migrations)
- Nginx default-server (v5.1.0+): unmatched Host on :80/:443 closed with 444; wildcard aliases (`cipi alias add '*.example.com'`)
- CrowdSec (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi crowdsec enable|disable|status|allow|unallow|rescue`; engine plus a registered firewall bouncer; rescue TLS listener with a one-shot break-glass token; not a WAF
- Integrity + malware scan (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi scan enable|disable|status|report|manifest|<app>`; nightly 04:40; sha256 vs the deploy manifest, then ClamAV on upload dirs only
- Shell completion (v5.2.0+): bash and zsh completion installed by `setup.sh` and every `self-update`; since 5.5.0 it works after `sudo cipi` with or without bash-completion, in `sudo -s`/`su`/tmux shells (`~/.bashrc` loader for root and cipi) and completes app names for the cipi user; `cipi completion bash|zsh [--print]` for another user or a custom rc file
- Search (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi search install|enable|disable|list|status|key|upgrade|remove` — native Meilisearch for Laravel Scout; 127.0.0.1 only; Cipi writes `SCOUT_PREFIX`; not in `cipi backup`
- Host packages (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi package list|install|remove` — allowlisted Ubuntu binaries (image-optimizers, ffmpeg, imagemagick, poppler-utils); Chromium refused
- Git forges (v5.2.3+): auto-setup for GitHub, GitLab, Cursor Origin, AWS CodeCommit, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps; `cipi git status|refresh|<provider>-token|remove-<provider>`
- Manual stack upgrades (v5.2.3+): `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [engine]`, `cipi service upgrade [nginx|mariadb|postgresql|valkey]` — patch-level, operator-triggered, never scheduled; the four packages kept off unattended-upgrades
- Cloudflare Zero Trust (v5.3.0+, opt-in): `cipi zt token|enable|disable|status|refresh|hostname|access|ssh|lock|unlock|origin-cert` — locally-managed tunnel, nginx real_ip, Cloudflare Access for staging/GUI/SSH, `lock http` / `lock ssh` to close the origin (both refuse when unsafe); fail2ban and UFW stay
- System monitor (v5.3.0+, on by default): `cipi monitor [--json]|list|enable|disable|set|test` — disk, per-app disk limits (`app_disk`, 5.5.0+), SSL expiry, services, workers, 5xx spikes, read-only fs, load every 5 minutes; alerts on state change, recovery and a reminder every 4h
- Alert channels (v5.3.0+): `cipi notifications channel add|list|test|enable|disable|remove` — Slack, Discord, Telegram, ntfy, JSON webhook for every notification trigger; best-effort, 5s timeout
- Compliance evidence (v5.3.1+, read-only): `cipi compliance [check] [--days=90] [--json]` runs 17 controls (ssh, firewall, intrusion, patching, kernel, tls, accounts, ssh_keys, api_tokens, gui_2fa, secrets, deploys, backups, logging, monitoring, time, malware) mapped to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A and SOC 2 TSC, exits 1 on any fail; `cipi compliance report [--out=] [--no-archive]` writes a root-only evidence bundle with SHA256SUMS; `list`, `controls`. Cipi itself cannot be certified — this is evidence for your audit
- Redirects (v5.3.1+): `cipi redirect set <app> --to=<url> [--301|--302|--307|--308] [--no-path]` (every name of the app in one hop, ACME kept public), `enable|disable|unset`; `cipi redirect add|remove|list <app>` for exact or prefix (trailing `/`) path redirects
- Proxy prefixes (v5.3.1+): `cipi proxy add <app> <prefix> <http(s)://upstream> [--strip-prefix] [--preserve-host] [--timeout=60] [--no-buffering] [--force]`, `remove`, `list` — WebSocket, X-Forwarded-* headers; loopback ports used by Cipi refused without --force; nginx -t failure restores apps.json and vhost
- Node apps (v5.4.0+): `cipi app create --node=spa|static|ssr [--framework=next|nuxt|sveltekit|astro|remix|vite]`; SSR blue/green with a health path; `cipi node install|list|upgrade|remove|default|status|restart|logs`; server-wide Node 22 default replaces end-of-life Node 20
- Disk usage (v5.5.0+): `cipi disk [--json]` — server filesystems then every app (files, database, total, % of disk, soft limit); `cipi disk db [--json]` — MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Valkey, Meilisearch in MB; `cipi app limits <app> --disk=<GB>|none` sets a soft limit watched by the `app_disk` monitor check (warn 90%, crit over, never blocks). Since 5.5.2 / API 1.33 the same JSON is `GET /api/disk` and `GET /api/disk/dbs` (`disk-view`); the soft limit is `GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/limits` since API 1.32
- SSH and brute force (v5.5.0+): `cipi firewall attempts [<1-100>|default]` sets fail2ban's failed-login threshold (default 3) in a drop-in updates never reset; `cipi ssh apps [enable|disable <app>|--all]` turns app users' SSH/SFTP from other machines off or on, deploys over ssh localhost unaffected
- DNS-01 accounts (v5.5.0+): `cipi ssl dns set --name=<account> --token=`, `cipi ssl install <app> --dns=cloudflare --account=<account> [--wildcard]`, `cipi ssl dns list|remove` — one token per Cloudflare account, each certificate renews with its own
- Wildcard / multi-tenant (v5.5.1+, guide https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#wildcard-domains): `cipi alias add <app> '*.example.com'` routes the subdomains, `cipi ssl install <app> --dns=cloudflare` issues example.com + *.example.com over DNS-01 (Cloudflare API token, Zone → DNS → Edit; proxy may stay on). Behind the Cloudflare proxy: SSL/TLS Full (strict), never Flexible (redirect loop). Without Cloudflare DNS Cipi cannot issue a wildcard: move DNS to Cloudflare (DNS only is fine), list subdomains as aliases (HTTP-01), or bring a certificate issued with another certbot DNS plugin under `--cert-name <primary domain>`. Alternative behind the proxy: `cipi zt origin-cert <app>` (Cloudflare Origin CA).
- Deploy audit (v5.4.0+): hash-chained root-only `/var/log/cipi/deploys.jsonl`, mirrored to syslog; `cipi deploy <app> --audit [--days=] [--json]`; verified origin/operator/IP kept apart from app `claimed` fields; checked by `cipi compliance deploys`
- Panel API (`cipi/api` 1.33.0; disk usage needs Cipi 5.5.2, the 1.31 routes still need 5.4.1): REST + 73 MCP tools; `GET /api/disk` and `GET /api/disk/dbs` (`disk-view`, Cipi 5.5.2+); `GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/limits` including `disk_limit_gb` and `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/ssl/dns` (API 1.32, Cipi 5.5.0+); app list/show `type` (`laravel`|`custom`|`node`); redirects (`/api/apps/{name}/redirect*`, `redirects-view|manage`), proxies (`/api/apps/{name}/proxies`, `proxies-view|manage`, never --force), Node apps on `POST|PUT /api/apps` (`node`, `framework`, `node_version`, `build`, `start`, `output`, `health_path`) plus `GET /api/node`, `GET /api/apps/{name}/node`, `POST /api/apps/{name}/node/restart` (`node-view|manage`), `GET /api/apps/{name}/deploy/audit` (`deploy-manage`), `GET /api/search` + `POST /api/apps/{name}/search/enable|disable` (`search-view|manage`), read-only `GET /api/packages|monitor|zt` (`packages-view`, `monitor-view`, `zt-view`), `POST /api/apps/{name}/fix-permissions`, wildcard primary domains; API 1.19 removed `DELETE /api/php/{version}`, `PUT /api/php/default`, `DELETE /api/dbs/{name}`, `PUT /api/dbs/engines/default` and the `dbs-delete` ability (CLI-only now); app `.env` / `auth.json` / Artisan / app-run / deploy-config (Cipi 5.0.3+); server cockpit — PHP install, SSH keys, services, SMTP, healthchecks, IP whitelist (Cipi 5.0.6+ / API 1.15+); `POST /api/apps` accepts `octane` and `engine`; list/show expose `octane`/`octane_port`; www + multi-engine DB endpoints (1.12+)
- PHP security patches: managed by Cipi (`cipi php upgrade`), not unattended-upgrades; weekly check Sunday 03:30 (v4.7.13+)
- nginx / MariaDB / PostgreSQL / Valkey patches: also off unattended-upgrades, but manual only — `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade`, `cipi service upgrade` (v5.2.3+)
- S3 backups: staging dir defaults to /var/tmp, not /tmp (v4.7.14+); override via backup.json tmpdir or CIPI_BACKUP_TMPDIR
- SMTP: send via system `/etc/msmtprc` only (AppArmor/setgid-safe); legacy `/etc/cipi/.msmtprc` removed (v4.7.22 / migrations 4.7.20–4.7.22)
- Deploy SSH: `~/.ssh` must be mode 700 (not group-writable); `cipi app create` enforces it; `cipi app delete` purges orphan users/homes (v4.7.19)
- Panel API on Ubuntu 25.10+/26.04: sudo-rs sudoers, read-only /etc/cipi guards, open_basedir for log helpers, empty DBs in `cipi db list` (v4.7.18 / migrations 4.7.15–4.7.18)
- Integrations: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps (auto webhook + deploy keys), Cursor Origin and AWS CodeCommit (deploy key only), custom Git via SSH, webhooks, MCP server for AI agents, native alert channels — Slack, Discord, Telegram, ntfy, webhook (v5.3.0+) — plus CI deploy-notification examples

## Docs

- [Documentation Index](https://cipi.sh/docs/): Full technical documentation hub
- [Getting Started](https://cipi.sh/docs/getting-started): Installation, requirements, quick start, tech stack, app structure
- [Cipi Agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent): Laravel package `cipi/agent` 2.0 — webhook deploys (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Azure DevOps, with audit-ledger claims), health check (release, commit, failed jobs, storage), in-app MCP server (MCP 2024-11-05 → 2026-07-28; 11 tools: health, app_info, deploy, deploy_status, logs, artisan, db_query, db_schema, env_check, cipi_yml, anonymizer; resources; secret redaction; `panel_*` tools via cipi/sdk), `php artisan cipi:yml validate|show|generate|example|schema` (same rules as the server), MySQL/PostgreSQL database anonymizer (consistent/unique fake values, truncate, gzip, `cipi:init-anonymize --scan`, `cipi:anonymize-audit`) — `cipi-cli db anonymize <app> --email <addr>` (cipi-cli 1.5.0+) requests a dump from the terminal via the Cipi API, `cipi-cli db anonymize download <signed url>` saves it ([GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/agent))
- [Apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/apps): Create, manage, and configure Laravel, Node (SPA / static / SSR, 5.4.0+) and custom applications; soft per-app disk limits (5.5.0+); one `laravel.log` per app (5.5.0+)
- [Deploy & CI/CD](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy): Zero-downtime deployments, deploy audit ledger (5.4.0+), cipi.yml reference, Git integration, CI/CD pipelines, notifications
- [Infrastructure](https://cipi.sh/docs/infrastructure): PHP, Node runtimes (`cipi node`, 5.4.0+), databases, SSL (several Cloudflare accounts for DNS-01, 5.5.0+; over the API since 1.32), disk usage per app and per database (`cipi disk`, 5.5.0+; `GET /api/disk` since 5.5.2 / API 1.33), `cipi firewall attempts` and `cipi ssh apps` (5.5.0+), redirects, proxy prefixes, backups, workers, firewall, CrowdSec, Cloudflare Zero Trust, system monitor, compliance evidence, Meilisearch, host packages, server management
- [CLI Client](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client): Remote `cipi-cli` — manage servers from the terminal via the REST API
- [PHP SDK](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk): `cipi/sdk` — call the panel API from PHP, Laravel, and other frameworks with a Sanctum token
- [Control Panel (GUI)](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui): Optional self-hosted web control panel (3.1) — Laravel, Node and custom apps (incl. Octane / engine), redirects and proxies, deploys and deploy audit, Meilisearch, databases, SSL, www, read-only Node runtimes / packages / monitor / Zero Trust, Server → Disk (API 1.33), 2FA/TOTP, multi-server ([GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/gui))
- [Advanced](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced): REST API (1.33.0 — disk usage, limits, DNS-01 accounts, plus the 1.31 surface), migrations 5.4.0/5.4.1/5.5.0/5.5.1/5.5.2, server sync, vault encryption, SMTP and chat alert channels, IP whitelist, log retention, advanced config
- [About Cipi](https://cipi.sh/docs/about): History, security model, design decisions, companion tools, comparisons
- [Companion tools](https://cipi.sh/docs/about#companion-tools): Optional MIT tools by the same author that work alongside Cipi — conn (SSH connection manager), Boogle (self-hosted exception tracking and uptime), Checkpoint (Laravel security audit), Hackly (authorized vulnerability and attack-surface scanning), Larapilot (spec-driven AI workflow for Laravel), IndieStats (privacy-friendly analytics), Johnny (self-hosted S3 storage on a VPS), init (local Laravel + Filament bootstrap)
- [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/cipi-yml): The per-app configuration file committed with the code — aliases, PHP and php.ini, extra databases, queue workers or Horizon, Laravel Reverb (5.1.2+), scheduler, healthcheck and backup profiles, post-deploy steps (5.2.3+), and since 5.4.0 the www redirect, basic auth, redirects, proxies, Meilisearch, recipe options, limits, forced HTTPS, required env names, crons and a Node app's build — reconciled with `cipi yml plan` / `cipi yml apply`. Since 5.5.2: `deploy.node_build`, `predeploy_snapshot`, `cipi yml generate --save`, and removal of backup profiles the file no longer lists

## API & CLI

- [Installation & Quick Start](https://cipi.sh/docs/getting-started#installation): Server requirements, setup script, post-install access
- [Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#cipi-api): Server REST API + MCP + Swagger — current package **1.33.0** (`cipi/api`, [release 1.33.0](https://github.com/cipi-sh/api/releases/tag/1.33.0), [GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/api))
- [CLI Client](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client): Remote terminal client (cipi-cli 1.6.0) for apps, deploys, SSL, databases incl. anonymized dumps via cipi/agent, PHP, services, SSH keys, SMTP, healthchecks, redirects/proxies, IP whitelist, disk usage (`disk`, `disk db`) and host insights
- [PHP SDK](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk): Composer package `cipi/sdk` for PHP and Laravel
- [WHMCS Module](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#whmcs): WHMCS provisioning module for billing automation
- [Agent — MCP Server](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent#agent-mcp): Model Context Protocol server inside the Laravel app (11 tools + panel tools, every current MCP revision)
- [Agent — cipi.yml tooling](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent#agent-yml): validate, inspect and generate cipi.yml locally with the server's own validator

- [fortrabbit Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-fortrabbit): Self-hosted, Laravel-first alternative to the fortrabbit PHP PaaS
- [Render Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-render): Self-hosted, fixed-cost alternative to Render for Laravel teams
- [20i Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-20i): Laravel deploy CLI alternative to 20i managed hosting
- [Sevalla Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-sevalla): Self-hosted alternative to Sevalla (Kinsta) for Laravel
- [Ploi Cloud Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi-cloud): Self-hosted alternative to Ploi Cloud (ploi.cloud), distinct from Ploi.io
- [Ploi Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi): Free, open-source alternative to Ploi.io with no deploy limits
- [Cleavr Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cleavr): Free, self-hosted alternative to Cleavr for Laravel teams
- [moss.sh Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-moss): Free, unlimited-deploy alternative to moss.sh
- [Kamal Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-kamal): Full server panel alternative to Kamal — native LEMP, not just Docker deploys
- [RunCloud Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-runcloud): Laravel-native, free alternative to RunCloud
- [ServerPilot Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-serverpilot): Laravel-native, free alternative to ServerPilot
- [CloudPanel Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cloudpanel): Laravel-first, CLI-driven alternative to CloudPanel
- [Coolify Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-coolify): Laravel-native, CLI-first alternative to Coolify for teams that prefer a native LEMP stack over Docker
- [Dokku Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-dokku): Laravel-first alternative to Dokku with full server provisioning
- [Easypanel Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-easypanel): Laravel-native alternative to Easypanel without Docker overhead
- [Vito Deploy Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-vito-deploy): CLI-first, single-binary alternative to Vito Deploy
- [cPanel Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cpanel): Lightweight, Laravel-native alternative to cPanel
- [DirectAdmin Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-directadmin): Free, Laravel-native alternative to DirectAdmin for dedicated VPS deploys
- [Plesk Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-plesk): Lightweight, Laravel-native alternative to Plesk
